input.question: Why can humans get used to sleep deprivation in the short run?
input.ground_truth: My understanding is that it is mostly to do with sleep cycles. That groggy feeling comes when you wake up in the middle of the deep stage of sleep (sorry my understanding is not very accurate) this is similar to why you can nap for 20 mins and feel great but an hour nap can leave you feeling crappy. When I am going to have a short sleep I use an app called sleepy time which tells me the ideal time to wake up. It doesn't stop me feeling fatigued at the end of the day but it definitely makes waking up easier. Disclaimer: me no science, me just me and me do what works.

Question: Why can humans get used to sleep deprivation in the short run?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy that needs batteries to work. When you first take out the batteries, the toy works really well. But if you keep playing with it and don’t put new batteries in, after a while the toy starts to move slower and not work as good.

Now, your brain is like that toy and sleep is like the batteries. When you don’t sleep enough (sleep deprivation), your brain still tries to work, but not as well as when it’s had rest.

At first, if you don’t sleep for one night, your brain can still work a little bit like normal because it’s used to working without much sleep sometimes (maybe when you’re excited or playing). This is called getting “used to it” for a short time. But after a while, your brain gets tired and can’t work as well anymore.

So, humans can work okay for a little while without enough sleep, but not forever!
